extracted.intended_audience: writers, literary critics, and students of rhetoric/creative writing
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for producing and judging 'the Sublime' in poetry and oratory — describing sources of sublimity, stylistic devices that produce it, and the vices that destroy it. Useful for poets, orators, and critics aiming for elevated style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of the Sublime
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The Sublime' is "a certain loftiness and excellence of language" which "takes the reader out of himself... acting with an imperious and irresistible force."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sublimity is an elevation of expression that compels universal admiration; it is not mere ornament but a powerful effect that transcends the reader's ordinary state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whether sublimity can be taught
rubrics_metrics.description: Questioned modestly: Sublimity originates in nature/genius, and cannot be reduced wholly to rule; yet art can aid the gifted author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Art instructs by example and practice — study, sympathy, and emulation of great poets can cultivate sublimity, but only when the author is receptive and abandons himself to his genius.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grandeur of Thought
rubrics_metrics.description: Grandeur of thought (nobility of soul) is a primary source of sublimity: lofty, generous, and expansive ideas naturally produce sublime expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate noble, wide-reaching ideas and choose circumstances that reveal elevated character; selection of striking circumstances, amplification, and imagination are practical ways to manifest grandeur of thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of the most striking circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Selecting the most striking, weighty, or significant circumstances enhances sublimity by directing attention to what is grand and consequential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer moments and details that magnify moral or emotional significance; avoid trivial or distracting particulars that diminish elevation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amplification (enlargement of thought)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amplification — expanding and magnifying an idea — contributes to sublimity by increasing scale and emphasis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use measured expansion to lift an idea; compare effective amplifications (e.g., Demosthenes vs. Cicero) as models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imitation of great models
rubrics_metrics.description: Imitation (in the sense of emulation) of great poets and orators helps the writer internalize sublimity without slavish copying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use masterpieces as beacons or judges: ask how Homer, Demosthenes, or other exemplars would judge your passage; emulate aims and standards rather than surface mannerisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: Vivid, apt imagery is a source of sublimity when it arises from grandeur of thought and conveys passion and scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer images that amplify the idea and move the imagination; avoid decorative or trivial metaphors that distract from the main elevation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of moving the passions
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to move and rouse the reader's passions is a source of sublimity (discussed separately by Longinus).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sublimity often coincides with genuine passion; technique should not substitute for authentic emotional force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures of speech as sources of sublimity
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain figures (adjuration, rhetorical question, asyndeton, hyperbaton, changes of number/person/tense, periphrasis) can produce sublimity when used rightly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ figures to intensify and conceal artifice (the 'art to conceal art'); misuse or excess reduces effect. Examples: adjuration for urgency, asyndeton for rapid force, rhetorical questions to engage and lift.

rubrics_metrics.name: The art to conceal art
rubrics_metrics.description: A mark of great style is making art appear natural — concealing the labor behind striking effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Devices should not call attention to themselves; technique must be subordinated to passion and thought so the effect seems spontaneous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graceful expression (choice of words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Graceful, appropriate diction supports sublimity; apt word choice and tasteful ornaments of style are essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer words that fit the thought and tone; avoid both pedantic rarities and flippant modern fancies. Familiar words can be powerful if used properly; improper familiar usage can be vulgar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ornaments of style (including use of familiar words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ornaments (figures, metaphors, accumulated images) and judicious use of familiar words can contribute to elegance and force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not mistake ornament for substance; the use of familiar words must be controlled to avoid triviality or anti-climax.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metaphor (accumulated and abused)
rubrics_metrics.description: Metaphor is powerful when it accumulates to amplify idea, but can be abused into tasteless conceits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use metaphors that enlarge thought; beware of forced, far-fetched comparisons and conceits (examples and critiques given, including Plato's criticized conceits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparisons and similes
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparisons and similes, when noble and apt, help exalt imagery and meaning; trivial or grotesque similes reduce dignity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select comparisons that illuminate scale and feeling; avoid mixed, petty, or merely decorative similitudes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyperbole
rubrics_metrics.description: Hyperbole magnifies and can be sublime if consonant with thought and passion; misplaced hyperbole is bombastic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use measured exaggeration aligned with genuine feeling; avoid empty inflation that signals insincerity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dignity and elevation of structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Structural elevation — modulation of syllables, sentence composition, and overall architecture — supports sublimity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend to rhythm, cadence (modulation of syllables), and composition (arrangement of clauses and parts) to achieve an elevated effect; structure must mirror grandeur of thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modulation of syllables (rhythm)
rubrics_metrics.description: A dignified rhythm and measured modulation of syllables contribute to the sublime effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid monotony or awkward beats; rhythm should aid the natural flow and elevation of the sentence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition (overall arrangement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The composition of parts — how clauses, sentences, and larger sections are arranged — affects sublimity by shaping momentum and emphasis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose to build and release tension; ensure parts cohere toward a grand effect rather than descending into jerky or broken clauses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vices opposed to the Sublime: Affectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Affectation — artificial, showy manner — opposes sublimity by substituting surface polish for genuine elevation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid mannerisms, forced prettiness, and writing that seeks novelty for its own sake; authenticity is required for sublimity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vices opposed to the Sublime: Bombast
rubrics_metrics.description: Bombast is sham passion and inflated phraseology that pretends to grandeur but lacks substance; it 'transcends the Sublime' and falls on the other side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware of pompous language, grand-sounding but empty constructions; Longinus gives many comic examples where inflated diction produces bathos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vices opposed to the Sublime: False sentiment and Frigid conceits
rubrics_metrics.description: False sentiment (insincere emotion) and frigid conceits (cold, sterile cleverness) destroy the warm passion needed for sublimity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure feeling is genuine and ideas are heartfelt; cleverness without conviction leads to triviality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vices destructive: Abuse of rhythm
rubrics_metrics.description: Abuse of rhythm (poor or forced cadences) undermines sublimity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid monotonous or mechanical rhythms, and be cautious of metrical tricks that call attention to themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vices destructive: Broken and jerky clauses
rubrics_metrics.description: Fragmented, awkward clause construction (broken or jerky clauses) interrupts the elevated flow required for sublimity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor smooth, well-balanced sentences that support cumulative force; disjointed phrasing reduces dignity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vices destructive: Undue prolixity
rubrics_metrics.description: Excessive wordiness or needless prolixity dissipates force and lowers the style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice selection and compression — prefer concentrated expression; long-windedness often leads to bathos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vices destructive: Improper use of familiar words and anti-climax
rubrics_metrics.description: Misuse of colloquial or familiar words and sequences that lead to anti-climax damage sublimity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control register shifts; avoid descending from lofty to trivial within a passage (anti-climax), which undermines earlier grandeur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection (choice and omission)
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection — the power to choose what to include and exclude — is essential: good selection manifests nobility of thought and avoids petty detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the most revealing, weighty materials; be willing to cut polished but irrelevant passages. Longinus emphasizes selection as key to dignity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conviction (sincerity of mind)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conviction — genuine belief and moral earnestness — is a core quality that underpins sublimity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid rhetorical show without conviction; true sublimity must come from a mind that believes and feels the things it expresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write for antiquity and posterity (judging by great models and future readers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discipline yourself by asking how great masters would judge your work and how posterity might receive it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the past (Homer, Demosthenes, etc.) as exemplars and imagine the future reader's response; this helps resist fashionable fancies and transient cleverness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final external canon: universal acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: The critic's final test for sublimity is broad acceptance: 'what is truly Sublime will always please, and please all readers.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek effects that survive different tastes and ages; rely on large public and lasting judgment rather than small coterie fashions.
